::: {.about-text}
## About The AI-Native Mind

I believe we are in the early chapters of a fundamental shift in how software gets built: not only faster code generation, but a rethinking of how engineering organizations operate when every developer works alongside AI agents.

I have spent 14+ years on this trajectory: distributed systems at CERN, developer tools at GitHub, and founding an AI startup as CTO ([WeGaw](https://wegaw.com/), backed by the European Space Agency). Today I am a Director at Microsoft for the Agentic SDLC, leading solution sales and go-to-market strategy: helping enterprises adopt AI-native software delivery.

I created [APM](https://github.com/microsoft/apm), Microsoft's open-source Agent Package Manager, now supported by [GitHub's Dependabot](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-dependabot-version-updates-support-agent-package-manager/) and by [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/apm/). I designed the PROSE specification for writing agent instructions that hold up. I wrote [The Agentic SDLC Handbook](https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/?utm_source=theainativemind), everything I have learned about making AI-native development work at scale. And I build [APMX](https://github.com/danielmeppiel/apmx), an independent, experimental runner for verifiable agentic software factories.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.inside #handbook}
::: {.wrap}
## What you will find in the handbook

::: {.inside-list}
1. **Why AI-native development is more than adopting a coding agent.** Copilot, Claude or Cursor change how one developer works. What engineering organizations need to change is bigger.
2. **The governance gap.** How productivity gains disappear when AI-generated code reaches review, compliance and architecture standards.
3. **Agent onboarding.** Patterns that treat coding agents like new hires, with context, standards and guardrails built in.
4. **The PROSE specification.** A framework for writing agent instructions that are precise, composable and version-controlled.
5. **A two-command implementation pattern.** `apm install`, then `apm compile`.
6. **The full method.** From one developer's setup to agent governance across an enterprise.
:::

## Projects

::: {.project-list}
- [APM](https://github.com/microsoft/apm){.project-name}. Microsoft's open-source Agent Package Manager: declares the skills, prompts and plugins your coding agents use as dependencies, pins them, and governs them with one org-wide policy.
- [APMX](https://github.com/danielmeppiel/apmx){.project-name}. An independent, experimental open-source runner for agentic software factories: runs Agent Contracts on your coding agent, writes the receipt and provides the gate at merge.
- [Agent Contracts & Receipts](https://github.com/danielmeppiel/agent-contracts){.project-name}. Format draft 0.1, open for comment: read the [spec](https://github.com/danielmeppiel/agent-contracts/tree/main/spec), join the [discussions](https://github.com/danielmeppiel/agent-contracts/discussions).
